subject: rewriting RStan Stan object due to label switching

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: rewriting RStan Stan object due to label switching
parts:
Marc Scott (a colleague of Vince Dories's) asked me to post this to the
list for him:

I have read some stan threads about dealing with label switching in mixture models, and I'm not asking you to help me with the label switching problem. Let's assume I've written code (and I have) that can find the correct permutation of labels for the parms of interest. My problem is in reassigning the results to a stan fit object.

In the function fixLabels, I extract: stanFit@sim$samples[[i]] for each chain i.
I then construct those variable names, like mu[1], mu[2] etc, and reference them well enough to permute a full copy of the ...@sim$samples list.

I then reassign those samples to a copy of the fit object in the global env (lines start ###***###):

fit_stanMix <- stan(model_code = stanMix,fit=NULL, model_name = "Mix", data = simdat, iter = 4000, chains = 3, sample_file = 'Mix.csv', verbose = TRUE)

fit_stanReMix <- fixLabels(fit_stanMix,pars=c("theta","mu","sigma","prob_comp"),2)

print(fit_stanMix,pars=c("theta","mu","sigma"))
###***###
fit_stanMix2 <- fit_stanMix
for (i in 1:3) {
fit_stanMix2@sim$samples[[i]] <- fit_stanReMix[[i]]
}
print(fit_stanMix2,pars=c("theta","mu","sigma"))

I've checked, and the reassignments WORKED. The means have moved into the right place so they are under the same name in each chain. Ie, mu[1] has the same mean, no matter what chain. Label switching solved!

The QUESTION IS: why do my traceplots() LOOK FINE, but the second print, above, or the stan_rhat call (not shown) FAIL(S) to take into consideration the new assignment I just did, that clearly worked, but....

I didn't just switch the NAMES of the sims, I actually assigned the values so the ordering of parms is exactly the same in each chain.

WHAT STAN OBJECT COMPONENT DID I LEAVE OUT?

messages.author: c08cc06af3be5854
messages.subject: Re: rewriting RStan Stan object due to label switching
parts: The source of the problem is a cache that rstan uses to speed things up, I presume.  When I use the option, use_cache=F with summary, the problem goes away.  If anyone knows how to "rewrite" the cache using altered values of the stanfit object, I'd be glad to hear about it.  -Marc

parts:
On Friday, December 2, 2016 at 9:14:32 PM UTC-5, Marc A Scott wrote:
The source of the problem is a cache that rstan uses to speed things up, I presume.  When I use the option, use_cache=F with summary, the problem goes away.  If anyone knows how to "rewrite" the cache using altered values of the stanfit object, I'd be glad to hear about it.  -Marc

Rewriting a stanfit object is fraught with peril, but if you (successfully) rewrite it before calling print() or summary(), then I would think that would have the same effect as not using the cache.

Ben
